A negative exponent does not make a number negative. It means take the reciprocal of the positive power. For nonzero a, a to the negative n equals one over a to the n.
Two to the negative three equals one divided by two cubed, which is one eighth. Five to the negative one equals one fifth.
Two squared divided by two to the fifth is two to the negative third by exponent subtraction. Canceling the common factors gives one eighth.
For equal bases, multiply by adding exponents. For a power raised to a power, multiply the exponents. Three to the negative two times three to the fifth is twenty-seven.
One third to the negative second becomes three squared, or nine. Invert the entire fraction, not only the numerator.
Six x to the negative two divided by three x cubed simplifies to two divided by x to the fifth. Remember that x cannot be zero.
Two x to the negative two y cubed divided by four x y to the negative one becomes y to the fourth divided by two x cubed. Subtract exponents separately.
Negative power means reciprocal. Combine exponents first, simplify fractions, and retain restrictions. Continue with eighteen practice problems and the five-question test.
